analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES SOX rolls; Teamviewer cuts guide; Apple guide light; Palantir beat & raise; Starlink, Boost, Echostar; US hardware preview
key_insights: US tech reversed early gains of about 1% to close sharply lower. SOX fell 3.4%, taking chipmakers' three-day losses to 12%, and the Nasdaq 100 is 10% below its peak. Semis remain below their 200-day moving average, optical names fell 7.5% and neoclouds fell 6%.
Momentum stocks lost 6.7% even though Treasury yields eased to 4.91%. The sell-off spread to Asia, with MSCI Asia Pacific down almost 1% and Kospi down almost 4%.

Desk flow was subdued. Asset managers were moderate net sellers, led by tech. Hedge funds were moderate net buyers through short covering. Semiconductor selling continued to meet little buying interest.

AI capex funding is back in focus: an Oracle raise, Meta reportedly considering at least $20bn of debt, Microsoft's $25bn bond sale on Thursday (its first US offering since 2017) and Alphabet's return to Europe's bond market. This raises questions about investors' capacity to absorb the supply. AMD and Arista report today.

GS Econ/GIR expects the focus on data centers in political campaigns to fade after the US election. A national data center moratorium looks unlikely in any election outcome. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, and the focus is likely to shift to AI regulation, where basic federal oversight is possible and restrictive regulation looks unlikely.

Apple's September quarter was strong but the stock fell 3% after hours on Services and margin guidance. Revenue rose 11.7% to $114.5bn, iPhone sales rose 17.5% to $57.6bn and EPS was $2.10 against consensus of $1.99. December revenue guidance of 8-10% growth compares with 6% consensus.

Apple's Services growth slowed to 9.8% versus 10.3% expected, its first single-digit quarter since June 2023. December Services guidance of 8-9% disappointed. App Store revenue was flat in September on softer mobile gaming, US link-outs, lower take rates and weaker third-party licensing.

Apple's December gross margin guidance of 45-46% missed consensus of 46.9%. Rising memory costs are expected to pressure margins for several quarters as cheaper inventory is used up. The CEO called memory pricing 'unprecedented' and said it is 'continuing to increase' after December. Hedge funds were short ahead of results on memory-cost and unit concerns.

TeamViewer missed expectations and cut full-year guidance. Revenue was 2% below consensus, ARR missed GIR estimates by 1%, EBITDA was 1% below and free cash flow was well below consensus. FY26 revenue is now guided to decline 1-2% at constant currency, versus prior growth of 0-3% and GIR/consensus of about 1% growth. The cut implies Q4 revenue growth of about -4% to 0%.

TeamViewer's cut reflects slower sales conversion and weaker retention, particularly in the Americas. Enterprise revenue grew about 5%, but management expects Q4 conversion to slow as the US midterm elections reduce visibility. SMB revenue fell about 5% versus GIR's forecast of a 3% decline. The adjusted EBITDA margin target of about 43% was maintained.

Palantir beat and raised but shares finished down 3.8% after reversing an initial after-hours gain, on booking deceleration and valuation. Revenue rose 96% to $2.31bn versus sellside consensus of $2.18bn. Q4 revenue guidance of $2.65bn (+88%) exceeded sellside consensus of $2.46bn. Full-year guidance rose by $378m to $8.53bn, a smaller raise than the $498m in 2Q.

Palantir's US commercial revenue grew 148% to $984m, beating consensus of $943m but missing investor expectations of $1.00-1.02bn. The full-year US commercial floor of more than $3.56bn also missed investor expectations, and US commercial total contract value fell 31% quarter-on-quarter. US government growth reaccelerated to 96%. Bears point to slower bookings at a valuation of about 75x calendar 2027.

Press reports say Boost could offer Starlink an MVNO route into US wireless, but network-access rights should not be assumed to transfer automatically. T-Mobile access is cited as running to 21 January 2027. AT&T's agreement restricts resale and allows termination on a change of control. A straightforward deal looks unlikely.

Speculation also covers SpaceX acquiring EchoStar, which holds roughly 2% of SpaceX's equity. SpaceX could in effect buy back its own shares at a discount while acquiring spectrum. Whether DISH Wireless's abandoned radios and antennas retain value is debated.

GS hardware preview for C3Q26 reiterates Buy on DELL, HPE and NTAP and Sell on HPQ. Investor debates center on the durability of enterprise IT spend into 2027 (bulls cite agentic AI and an infrastructure refresh, bears cite memory cost inflation and demand pull-forward) and on neocloud demand sustainability, including a possible shift to white-box procurement.

Per the FT, Nvidia told data-centre clients to reduce China exposure, building on tighter customer checks in Singapore, Malaysia and Japan. Near-term revenue impact is likely limited given minimal China data-centre exposure, but it adds headline risk.

onsemi 3Q revenue was $1.72bn, in line with GS and the Street at $1.71bn, with EPS just above and guidance just above. GS expects the stock to be range bound. Datacentre power is strong while supply constraints are softening automotive. onsemi plans to acquire Ferric for $600mn in cash.
Counterpoint reports global smartphone SoC shipments fell 21% YoY in 3Q26 on rising memory costs, longer replacement cycles and cautious inventory management.

Digitimes reports Musk is considering letting TSMC operate his planned Texas Terafab, which would reverse his ambition to run chipmaking independently. The author says they would be surprised. Talks reportedly include TSMC and Intel.
A second wave of cyberattacks is suspected to have hit supermarket refrigerators across Europe. Ahold and Colruyt confirmed the hacks.

BBVA is moving toward exiting Telefónica, having cut its stake from 5% to 1.96% and using derivatives to unwind the rest. OpenAI signed ad deals with Magnite and PubMatic. Auto1 October data shows inventory turns improving, with the implied 4Q26 sales run-rate about 3% below consensus.

earnings_insights: Apple reported September quarter revenue of $114.5bn (+11.7%) against consensus, with reported EPS of $2.10 versus consensus of $1.99. Gross margin was 47.9% reported, or 46.9% excluding a one-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds. Services growth was 9.8% versus 10.3% expected.
Apple guided December revenue growth of 8-10% versus consensus of 6%, Services growth of 8-9%, and gross margin of 45-46% versus consensus of 46.9%.

Palantir reported revenue of $2.31bn (+96%) versus sellside consensus of $2.18bn and buyside expectations of $2.30-2.34bn. Q4 revenue guidance is $2.65bn versus sellside consensus of $2.46bn. US commercial revenue was $984m (+148%) versus consensus of $943m.

TeamViewer reported revenue 2% below consensus, with pro forma adjusted EBITDA margin of 42.8% versus GIR/consensus of 42.7%/42.6%. FY26 revenue is guided to -1% to -2% at constant currency, down from 0-3% growth.
onsemi reported 3Q revenue of $1.72bn versus GS at $1.72bn and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.71bn. EPS was just above the Street and guidance was just above.
AMD and Arista report today. GS hardware C3Q26 previews cover DELL, HPE, NTAP and HPQ.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors see a structural uplift in demand for traditional compute, storage and data centre networking from agentic AI and an infrastructure refresh, which should be a durable multi-year driver despite elevated ASPs.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors attribute 2026 industry revenue strength to memory cost inflation and demand pull-forward, and see OEMs over-earning on server and storage, with margin downside if memory pricing slows or reverses.

tension_points.bull_case: US server and networking OEMs' design, supply-chain, integration and deployment capabilities are a moat versus ODMs and justify premium pricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Neoclouds could shift to cloud-like white-box procurement for compute, networking and storage.
